sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by FCM in two independent cell lines (MC38 and HCT116); NKG2D-ligand function of the tagged construct was NOT MEASURED explicitly for the tagged protein.
sites.rationale: MICA is a type I single-pass membrane protein with its N-terminus extracellular (after SP cleavage at residue 23) and its C-terminus intracellular. FCM detection of surface EGFP fluorescence without permeabilization uniquely identifies the extracellular N-terminus as the fusion site, because a C-terminal EGFP would be cytoplasmic and invisible to surface FCM. There is therefore exactly one extracellular terminus, making this a topology_derived position: insert_after_residue = 23 (last SP residue, A), placing the tag between A23 and E24 (the mature N-terminus). Computed distance from the junction to the TM boundary is 284 residues, well clear of any TM proximity constraint. Full-length MICA (allele 001) fused to EGFP was stably expressed in MC38 and HCT116 tumor cell lines via lentiviral transduction. Surface display of the EGFP-tagged construct was confirmed by flow cytometry (FCM) in both cell lines, with wild-type cells as negative controls (L2, L3). No residue number is stated in the ledger; the junction is derived from topology.

sources.claim: (E–G) EGFP + MC38 cells stably expressing human full-length MICA or MICA Δα1/2 were validated by FCM (wild-type MC38 cells as negative controls) (E) and injected into C57BL/6 mice ( n = 6 per group) via the tail vein.

literature_notes: L1 describes a commercial lentiviral vector from Cyagen Biosciences with no stated tag position and therefore does not independently qualify as a pinned site per the ledger rules. L2 and L3 report the experimental result — surface FCM confirmation of EGFP-tagged full-length MICA in two cell lines — and do qualify as evidence of a tolerated insertion in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct. Because no residue number is given in any ledger line, the junction is topology_derived: MICA's single extracellular terminus (N-terminal, after SP cleavage) is the only location consistent with surface FCM detection of EGFP. The Δα1/2 deletion variant mentioned in the same papers is a truncated construct and does not provide an additional independent site. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
